value: 31B Dense model: 30.7B total parameters, 60 layers, 1024-token sliding window, 256K context, 262K vocabulary. It uses a hybrid attention mechanism interleaving local sliding window attention with full global attention (final layer always global), to deliver the speed and low memory footprint of a lightweight model without sacrificing deep awareness for complex long-context tasks. Global layers use unified Keys and Values and Proportional RoPE (p-RoPE) to optimize memory for long contexts.
quote:
The models employ a hybrid attention mechanism that interleaves local sliding window attention with full global attention, ensuring the final layer is always global. This hybrid design delivers the processing speed and low memory footprint of a lightweight model without sacrificing the deep awareness required for complex, long-context tasks. value: The card acknowledges that VLMs trained on large-scale real-world text and image data can reflect socio-cultural biases. Mitigation: careful scrutiny, input data pre-processing, and post-training evaluations. It also notes that biases or gaps in training data can limit responses, and encourages continuous monitoring (evaluation metrics, human review) and exploration of de-biasing techniques.
quote: VLMs trained on large-scale, real-world text and image data can reflect socio-cultural biases embedded in the training material. Gemma 4 models underwent careful scrutiny, input data pre-processing, and post-training evaluations as reported in this card to help mitigate the risk of these biases. [...] Biases or gaps in the training data can lead to limitations in the model's responses. [...] **Perpetuation of biases**: It's encouraged to perform continuous monitoring (using evaluation metrics, human review) and the exploration of de-biasing techniques during model training, fine-tuning, and other use cases.
quotes: VLMs trained on large-scale, real-world text and image data can reflect socio-cultural biases embedded in the training material. value: The card gives rationale for some design choices. Hybrid attention (local sliding window interleaved with global attention) gives the speed and low memory footprint of a lightweight model without losing awareness for long-context tasks. Global layers use unified Keys and Values and p-RoPE to optimize memory for long contexts. Training data includes code so the model learns programming syntax and patterns, and includes mathematical text to help it learn logical reasoning.
quote: This hybrid design delivers the processing speed and low memory footprint of a lightweight model without sacrificing the deep awareness required for complex, long-context tasks. [...] To optimize memory for long contexts, global layers feature unified Keys and Values, and apply Proportional RoPE (p-RoPE). [...] Exposing the model to code helps it to learn the syntax and patterns of programming languages, which improves its ability to generate code and understand code-related questions. [...] Training on mathematical text helps the model learn logical reasoning, symbolic representation, and to address mathematical queries.
quotes: This hybrid design delivers the processing speed and low memory footprint of a lightweight model without sacrificing the deep awareness required for complex, long-context tasks.
To optimize memory for long contexts, global layers feature unified Keys and Values, and apply Proportional RoPE (p-RoPE).
Exposing the model to code helps it to learn the syntax and patterns of programming languages, which improves its ability to generate code and understand code-related questions.
Training on mathematical text helps the model learn logical reasoning, symbolic representation, and to address mathematical queries.

value: Intended uses include content creation and communication (text generation, chatbots and conversational AI, text summarization, image data extraction, audio processing and interaction for E2B, E4B, and 12B models) and research and education (NLP and VLM research, language learning tools, knowledge exploration). The card says the list is not comprehensive.
quote: The following list of potential uses is not comprehensive. [...] **Text Generation**: These models can be used to generate creative text formats such as poems, scripts, code, marketing copy, and email drafts. [...] **Chatbots and Conversational AI**: Power conversational interfaces for customer service, virtual assistants, or interactive applications. [...] **Text Summarization**: Generate concise summaries of a text corpus, research papers, or reports. [...] **Image Data Extraction**: These models can be used to extract, interpret, and summarize visual data for text communications. [...] **Audio Processing and Interaction**: The E2B, E4B, and 12B models can analyze and interpret audio inputs, enabling voice-driven interactions and transcriptions. [...] **Natural Language Processing (NLP) and VLM Research**: These models can serve as a foundation for researchers to experiment with VLM and NLP techniques, develop algorithms, and contribute to the advancement of the field. [...] **Language Learning Tools**: Support interactive language learning experiences, aiding in grammar correction or providing writing practice.
quotes: The following list of potential uses is not comprehensive.
**Text Generation**: These models can be used to generate creative text formats such as poems, scripts, code, marketing copy, and email drafts.
**Chatbots and Conversational AI**: Power conversational interfaces for customer service, virtual assistants, or interactive applications.
**Text Summarization**: Generate concise summaries of a text corpus, research papers, or reports.
**Image Data Extraction**: These models can be used to extract, interpret, and summarize visual data for text communications.
**Audio Processing and Interaction**: The E2B, E4B, and 12B models can analyze and interpret audio inputs, enabling voice-driven interactions and transcriptions.

**Natural Language Processing (NLP) and VLM Research**: These models can serve as a foundation for researchers to experiment with VLM and NLP techniques, develop algorithms, and contribute to the advancement of the field.
**Language Learning Tools**: Support interactive language learning experiences, aiding in grammar correction or providing writing practice.

value: Use with the latest Transformers library (pip install -U transformers torch accelerate), loading via AutoProcessor and AutoModelForMultimodalLM, with chat template via processor.apply_chat_template using system/user roles; thinking enabled via enable_thinking=True or the <|think|> token at start of system prompt; output parsed with processor.parse_response. Card notes libraries like Transformers and llama.cpp handle the chat template.
quote: You can use all Gemma 4 models with the latest version of Transformers. To get started, install the necessary dependencies in your environment: [...] `pip install -U transformers torch accelerate` [...] from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForMultimodalLM [...] To enable reasoning, set `enable_thinking=True` and the `parse_response` function will take care of parsing the thinking output. [...] **Trigger Thinking:** Thinking is enabled by including the `<|think|>` token at the start of the system prompt. To disable thinking, remove the token. [...] Note that many libraries like Transformers and llama.cpp handle the complexities of the chat template for you.
quotes: You can use all Gemma 4 models with the latest version of Transformers. To get started, install the necessary dependencies in your environment:
`pip install -U transformers torch accelerate`
from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForMultimodalLM
To enable reasoning, set `enable_thinking=True` and the `parse_response` function will take care of parsing the thinking output.
**Trigger Thinking:** Thinking is enabled by including the `<|think|>` token at the start of the system prompt. To disable thinking, remove the token.
Note that many libraries like Transformers and llama.cpp handle the complexities of the chat template for you.

Gemma 4 models were developed with internal safety and responsible AI teams and underwent automated and human evaluations aligned with Google's AI principles and safety policies. Results: major improvements in all content safety categories relative to previous Gemma models; significantly outperform Gemma 3 and 3n in safety while keeping unjustified refusals low; minimal policy violations for text-to-text and image-to-text across all model sizes. Testing was conducted without safety filters.
quote: Gemma 4 models were developed in partnership with internal safety and responsible AI teams. A range of automated as well as human evaluations were conducted to help improve model safety. [...] For all areas of safety testing, we saw major improvements in all categories of content safety relative to previous Gemma models. Overall, Gemma 4 models significantly outperform Gemma 3 and 3n in improving safety, while keeping unjustified refusals low. All testing was conducted without safety filters to evaluate the model capabilities and behaviors. [...] For both text-to-text and image-to-text, and across all model sizes, the model produced minimal policy violations, and showed significant improvements over previous Gemma models' performance.
